title: Verify Navigation to Functional Test Insights View
description: Verify that users can successfully navigate to the new Functional Test Insights view from the main dashboard
testDescription: This test validates that a user can access the Functional Test Insights view by navigating from the main dashboard, and that the view loads correctly with all expected UI components.
prerequisites:
1. User is logged into the system with appropriate permissions.
2. Playwright tests have been executed and results are available in the system.
3. Insights view for Unit, Integration, and API tests are already implemented and working.
stepsToPerform:
1. Navigate to the main dashboard page.
2. Locate and click on the 'Test Insights' or equivalent navigation element.
3. Verify that a tab or option for 'Functional Tests' is available.
4. Click on the 'Functional Tests' tab/option.
5. Wait for the page to load completely.
expectedResult:
1. Functional Tests Insights view should load successfully.
2. The page title should indicate 'Functional Test Insights' or equivalent.
3. Navigation breadcrumb should reflect the current location.
4. All UI components (filters, test list, summary statistics) should be visible.
5. The layout should be consistent with existing Unit, Integration, and API test views.
testData: N/A - Navigation test
automationNotes: Use Playwright's page.goto() and navigation methods. Implement proper wait strategies for page loading. Verify UI elements using expect() assertions.
testArtifacts: Screenshots of successful navigation to the Functional Tests view

title: Verify Display and Functionality of Test Results in Insights View
description: Verify that Playwright functional test results are correctly displayed with proper status indicators and that detailed information can be accessed
testDescription: This test validates that Playwright test results are correctly displayed in the Insights view with appropriate status indicators (passed, failed, skipped), and that users can access detailed test information by interacting with the results.
prerequisites:
1. User is logged into the system.
2. Multiple Playwright functional tests have been executed with various statuses (passed, failed, skipped).
3. User has navigated to the Functional Test Insights view.
stepsToPerform:
1. Observe the list of functional test results displayed in the Insights view.
2. Verify that each test result shows a clear status indicator (passed, failed, skipped).
3. Click on a passed test to expand its details.
4. Examine the information displayed for the passed test.
5. Close or collapse the passed test details.
6. Click on a failed test to expand its details.
7. Examine the information displayed for the failed test, including error messages and stack traces.
8. Check for the presence of test artifacts (screenshots, videos) for the failed test.
expectedResult:
1. Test results should be displayed in a clear, organized format.
2. Status indicators should be visually distinct (e.g., green for passed, red for failed, gray for skipped).
3. Expanding a test should reveal detailed information about the test execution.
4. Passed tests should show execution time, browser information, and other relevant details.
5. Failed tests should display error messages, stack traces, and links to test artifacts.
6. Test artifacts (screenshots, videos, traces) should be accessible and load correctly when accessed.
testData: Test results with various statuses (passed, failed, skipped)
automationNotes: Use page.locator() to find and interact with test result elements. Verify expanded details using expect(). Check that artifacts are accessible using page.isVisible() for artifact links.
testArtifacts: Screenshots of test results in various states (collapsed/expanded), screenshots of artifact displays

title: Verify Filtering and Sorting Functionality in Functional Test Insights
description: Verify that users can filter and sort functional test results based on various criteria
testDescription: This test validates that users can filter and sort Playwright test results in the Insights view based on criteria such as test status, execution time, browser, and test name, and that the filtered/sorted results are accurately displayed.
prerequisites:
1. User is logged into the system.
2. Multiple Playwright functional tests with diverse characteristics (status, duration, browser) have been executed.
3. User has navigated to the Functional Test Insights view.
stepsToPerform:
1. Locate the filtering options in the Insights view.
2. Apply a filter to show only failed tests and verify the results.
3. Clear the filter and apply a new filter to show only tests executed in Chrome.
4. Apply multiple filters simultaneously (e.g., failed tests in Chrome).
5. Clear all filters.
6. Locate the sorting options in the Insights view.
7. Sort tests by execution time (ascending) and verify the order.
8. Sort tests by name (alphabetical) and verify the order.
9. Sort tests by status and verify the order.
expectedResult:
1. Filtering options should be clearly visible and functional.
2. When a filter is applied, only matching test results should be displayed.
3. Multiple filters should work in combination (logical AND).
4. Clearing filters should restore the full list of test results.
5. Sorting options should be clearly visible and functional.
6. When sorting is applied, test results should be ordered correctly according to the selected criterion.
7. The current filter and sort selections should be visually indicated to the user.
testData: Test results with various statuses, execution times, and browsers
automationNotes: Use Playwright's interaction methods (click, fill, select) to apply filters and sorting. Verify filtered/sorted results using expect() assertions on the displayed data.
testArtifacts: Screenshots of filter application and sorting results

title: Verify Integration with Existing Test Insights Views
description: Verify that the Functional Test Insights view integrates properly with existing Unit, Integration, and API test insights views
testDescription: This test validates that the new Functional Test Insights view integrates seamlessly with the existing insights views for Unit, Integration, and API tests, maintaining consistent navigation, UI patterns, and functionality across all test types.
prerequisites:
1. User is logged into the system.
2. All types of tests (Unit, Integration, API, and Functional) have been executed and have results available.
3. User has appropriate permissions to view all test types.
stepsToPerform:
1. Navigate to the main Test Insights dashboard.
2. Switch from the default view to the Unit Tests view.
3. Note the UI layout, components, and functionality.
4. Switch to the Integration Tests view.
5. Verify consistency with the Unit Tests view.
6. Switch to the API Tests view.
7. Verify consistency with previous views.
8. Switch to the new Functional Tests view.
9. Verify consistency with all previous views.
10. Navigate back and forth between different test type views several times.
expectedResult:
1. Navigation between different test type views should be smooth and intuitive.
2. UI components (filters, sorting options, test list layout, details view) should be consistent across all test type views.
3. Common functionality (filtering, sorting, expanding test details) should work similarly across all views.
4. Visual design elements (colors, icons, typography) should be consistent across all views.
5. State should be preserved when navigating away from and back to a specific view (e.g., filter selections should be maintained).
6. Performance should be comparable when loading different test type views.
testData: Results for all test types (Unit, Integration, API, Functional)
automationNotes: Use Playwright to navigate between different views and verify consistency of elements and functionality. Take screenshots of each view for visual comparison.
testArtifacts: Screenshots of each test type view for comparison, recordings of navigation between views

title: Verify Test Artifacts Accessibility in Functional Test Insights View
description: Verify that Playwright test artifacts (screenshots, videos, traces) are correctly linked and accessible from the Functional Test Insights view
testDescription: This test validates that Playwright-specific test artifacts such as screenshots, videos, and traces are correctly linked in the Functional Test Insights view and can be accessed and viewed by users, especially for failed tests where these artifacts are critical for debugging.
prerequisites:
1. User is logged into the system.
2. Playwright tests have been executed that generated various artifacts:
   - Screenshots (automatic on failure and manual)
   - Videos of test execution
   - Playwright traces
3. User has navigated to the Functional Test Insights view.
stepsToPerform:
1. Locate and click on a failed test in the Functional Test Insights view.
2. Examine the expanded test details for links to test artifacts.
3. Click on a screenshot link/thumbnail and verify it opens correctly.
4. Return to the test details.
5. Click on a video recording link and verify it plays correctly.
6. Return to the test details.
7. Click on a trace link and verify the trace viewer opens correctly.
8. Attempt to download each artifact type and verify the download is successful.
9. Repeat the artifact checks for different browsers (if artifacts exist for multiple browsers).
expectedResult:
1. Test artifacts should be clearly indicated and accessible from the test details view.
2. Screenshots should open in an appropriate viewer or modal within the application.
3. Videos should play correctly in an embedded player or appropriate external viewer.
4. Traces should open in the Playwright Trace Viewer or equivalent.
5. Downloads of artifacts should complete successfully and the downloaded files should be valid and viewable.
6. All artifacts should be correctly associated with the specific test run they belong to.
7. Artifacts should be available for different browsers as appropriate.
testData: Failed tests with various artifacts (screenshots, videos, traces)
automationNotes: Use Playwright to navigate to and interact with artifact links. For verification, check that viewers/modals open (isVisible()) and that downloads complete successfully. May need to handle new tabs/windows for some artifact viewers.
testArtifacts: Screenshots of artifact links in test details, screenshots of opened artifacts in viewers

title: Verify Dashboard Summary Statistics for Functional Tests
description: Verify that the dashboard displays accurate summary statistics for Playwright functional tests
testDescription: This test validates that the Functional Test Insights view displays accurate summary statistics including total tests, pass/fail rates, average execution time, and trends over time.
prerequisites:
1. User is logged into the system with appropriate permissions.
2. Multiple Playwright functional tests have been executed over several days/weeks.
3. User has navigated to the Functional Test Insights view.
stepsToPerform:
1. Observe the summary statistics section of the Functional Tests Insights dashboard.
2. Verify the displayed count of total tests matches the actual number of tests.
3. Check that the pass/fail percentages accurately reflect the test results.
4. Verify the average execution time statistic.
5. Locate and examine the trends visualization (chart/graph).
6. Hover over data points in the trends visualization to view detailed information.
7. If available, change the time period for the summary (e.g., last 7 days, last 30 days).
8. Compare refreshed statistics with the expected values for the selected time period.
expectedResult:
1. Summary statistics should be prominently displayed and visually appealing.
2. Test count should match the actual number of functional tests in the system.
3. Pass/fail percentages should accurately reflect the current test results.
4. Average execution time should be calculated correctly.
5. Trends visualization should show changes in test metrics over time.
6. Tooltips or popovers on hover should provide detailed information for data points.
7. Changing the time period should update all statistics and visualizations appropriately.
8. All numerical values should be formatted consistently with appropriate units.
testData: Historical test execution results spanning multiple days/weeks
automationNotes: Use page.locator() to find summary elements and expect() to verify numerical values. For hover interactions, use page.hover(). May need to parse text content and compare with calculated expected values.

title: Verify Search Functionality for Functional Test Results
description: Verify that users can search for specific functional tests using various search criteria
testDescription: This test validates that users can search for specific Playwright functional tests using various criteria such as test name, description, error message, and status, and that search results are accurately displayed.
prerequisites:
1. User is logged into the system.
2. A large number of Playwright functional tests with diverse characteristics have been executed.
3. User has navigated to the Functional Test Insights view.
stepsToPerform:
1. Locate the search functionality in the Functional Tests Insights view.
2. Enter a specific test name in the search field and submit.
3. Verify that matching tests are displayed in the results.
4. Clear the search and enter a partial test name.
5. Verify that all tests containing the search term are displayed.
6. Search for a specific error message that appears in failed tests.
7. Verify that only failed tests with that error message are displayed.
8. Test case-insensitive search by entering mixed-case search terms.
9. Test searching by test description or other metadata.
10. Clear all search criteria and verify full list is restored.
expectedResult:
1. Search functionality should be easily accessible and intuitive.
2. Exact match searches should return precisely matching results.
3. Partial match searches should return all tests containing the search term.
4. Searching by error message should find relevant failed tests.
5. Searches should be case-insensitive by default.
6. Results should be displayed quickly, even with large test sets.
7. Search criteria should be clearly indicated while active.
8. Search results should maintain all normal functionality (expanding details, etc.).
9. A "no results found" message should display when no matches are found.
10. Clearing search should restore the full list of tests.
testData: Large set of test results with various names, descriptions, and error messages
automationNotes: Use page.fill() to enter search terms and page.click() for search submission. Verify results using expect() assertions on the visible test items. Test edge cases like empty search, special characters, and very long search terms.

title: Verify Export and Reporting Capabilities for Functional Tests
description: Verify that users can export functional test results in various formats for reporting purposes
testDescription: This test validates that users can export Playwright functional test results in various formats (CSV, PDF, JSON) and that the exported data is complete, properly formatted, and contains all relevant test information.
prerequisites:
1. User is logged into the system with appropriate permissions.
2. Multiple Playwright functional tests have been executed with various statuses.
3. User has navigated to the Functional Test Insights view.
stepsToPerform:
1. Locate the export or reporting functionality in the Functional Tests Insights view.
2. Select CSV as the export format and initiate the export.
3. Verify the download completes and open the CSV file to check content.
4. Return to the Insights view and select PDF as the export format.
5. Configure any available PDF options (if applicable) and initiate the export.
6. Verify the PDF download completes and open the file to check content.
7. Return to the Insights view and select JSON as the export format.
8. Verify the JSON download completes and check the file content.
9. Apply filters to show only a subset of tests (e.g., only failed tests).
10. Export the filtered results and verify that only the filtered tests are included.
expectedResult:
1. Export functionality should be easily accessible.
2. CSV exports should include all relevant test data in properly formatted columns.
3. PDF exports should be well-formatted with appropriate styling and organization.
4. JSON exports should contain complete test data in valid JSON format.
5. All exports should include test names, statuses, execution times, and other relevant metadata.
6. For failed tests, exports should include error information.
7. Exports of filtered results should only include the tests shown in the filtered view.
8. Export files should be named appropriately, potentially including the date and filter criteria.
9. Large exports should complete in a reasonable time.
10. Progress indication should be provided for time-consuming exports.
testData: Complete set of test results with various statuses
automationNotes: Use Playwright's download handling capabilities to verify downloads complete successfully. For content verification, may need to read and parse downloaded files. Test with both small and large data sets to verify performance.

title: Verify Test Execution History and Comparison View
description: Verify that users can view and compare test execution history across multiple runs
testDescription: This test validates that users can access historical execution data for Playwright functional tests, view trends over time, and compare results across different test runs to identify patterns or regressions.
prerequisites:
1. User is logged into the system.
2. Multiple runs of the same Playwright functional tests have been executed over time.
3. User has navigated to the Functional Test Insights view.
stepsToPerform:
1. Locate the test history or comparison functionality in the Insights view.
2. Select a specific test that has been run multiple times.
3. View the execution history for that test, showing status across multiple runs.
4. Identify a test that has changed status (passed to failed or vice versa).
5. Access the comparison view for two different runs of the same test.
6. Examine the detailed differences between the two test runs.
7. Check for visual indicators of performance changes across runs (execution time).
8. Verify the ability to navigate to specific historical test runs.
9. If available, use timeline visualization to see patterns over time.
10. Check that historical artifacts (screenshots, videos) are accessible for past runs.
expectedResult:
1. Test execution history should be clearly visualized showing status across runs.
2. Status changes between runs should be highlighted or easily identifiable.
3. Comparison view should clearly indicate differences between selected runs.
4. Execution time trends should be visible to identify performance degradation.
5. Historical test data should be complete, including execution environment details.
6. Navigation between current and historical runs should be intuitive.
7. Historical artifacts should be accessible and properly linked to their specific runs.
8. Timeline visualization (if available) should accurately represent test stability over time.
9. Date and time information for historical runs should be clearly displayed.
10. Historical data should load within reasonable time even with many past executions.
testData: Multiple runs of the same tests across different time periods, including tests with changing statuses
automationNotes: Use Playwright to interact with history views and comparison tools. Verify correct historical data display using expect() assertions. May need to set up specific test history data before execution.

title: Verify Accessibility Compliance of Functional Test Insights View
description: Verify that the Functional Test Insights view complies with accessibility standards and works properly with assistive technologies
testDescription: This test validates that the Functional Test Insights view complies with WCAG 2.1 accessibility standards, is usable with screen readers and keyboard navigation, and provides appropriate semantic markup and ARIA attributes.
prerequisites:
1. User is logged into the system.
2. Playwright functional tests have been executed and results are available.
3. User has navigated to the Functional Test Insights view.
stepsToPerform:
1. Run Playwright's built-in accessibility audit tools on the Functional Tests Insights view.
2. Verify that all interactive elements have appropriate keyboard focus indicators.
3. Test complete keyboard navigation through all functionality (no mouse required).
4. Verify that screen reader announces all important elements and states correctly.
5. Check color contrast ratios for all text elements against their backgrounds.
6. Verify that all images and icons have appropriate alt text or aria-label attributes.
7. Test that expanded/collapsed states are properly communicated to assistive technologies.
8. Verify that error states and notifications are announced by screen readers.
9. Check that dynamic content updates are properly announced to screen readers.
10. Test zoom functionality up to 200% to ensure layout remains usable.
expectedResult:
1. Accessibility audit should pass with no critical issues.
2. All interactive elements should have visible focus indicators when navigating with keyboard.
3. Complete functionality should be accessible using only keyboard navigation.
4. Screen readers should correctly announce all UI elements, their roles, and states.
5. All text should meet WCAG 2.1 AA contrast requirements (4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text).
6. Images and icons should have appropriate alternative text.
7. ARIA attributes should be correctly implemented for custom controls.
8. Expanded/collapsed states should be communicated via aria-expanded or similar attributes.
9. Dynamic content updates should use appropriate ARIA live regions.
10. Layout should remain functional when zoomed to 200%.
testData: Test results with various statuses and content types
automationNotes: Use Playwright's accessibility testing capabilities including page.accessibility.snapshot(). Test keyboard navigation using keyboard.press(). For screen reader testing, may need additional tools or manual verification.

title: Verify Performance Metrics Visualization in Functional Tests Insights
description: Verify that performance metrics for Playwright functional tests are correctly visualized and provide meaningful insights
testDescription: This test validates that the Functional Tests Insights view accurately displays performance metrics including test duration, resource usage, and load times in visual formats that help users identify performance trends and issues.
prerequisites:
1. User is logged into the system with appropriate permissions.
2. Multiple Playwright functional tests have been executed with performance metrics recorded.
3. User has navigated to the Functional Test Insights view.
stepsToPerform:
1. Locate the performance metrics section in the Functional Tests Insights view.
2. Verify that test duration metrics are displayed in graphical format (bar charts, line graphs).
3. Examine resource usage visualizations (CPU, memory) if available.
4. Check for page load time metrics and their visualization.
5. Interact with visualization controls (zoom, pan, filter by date range).
6. Hover over specific data points to view detailed metrics.
7. If available, compare performance across different browsers.
8. Identify tests with performance outliers (significantly longer execution times).
9. Verify that performance threshold indicators are visible (if implemented).
expectedResult:
1. Performance metrics should be clearly visualized using appropriate chart types.
2. Charts should be interactive, allowing users to explore data points.
3. Hovering over data points should reveal detailed metrics information.
4. Performance outliers should be visually highlighted or easily identifiable.
5. Performance thresholds (if defined) should be indicated on the visualizations.
6. Cross-browser performance comparison should be available and clearly presented.
7. All visualizations should be properly labeled with axes, titles, and units.
8. Performance trend lines should accurately reflect the underlying data.
9. Performance data should be consistent with actual test execution metrics.
testData: Test results with various performance characteristics and execution times
automationNotes: Use Playwright to interact with chart elements and verify visualizations. For data validation, may need to compare displayed values with known performance metrics from test results.

title: Verify User Customization Options for Functional Test Insights View
description: Verify that users can customize the display and behavior of the Functional Test Insights view according to their preferences
testDescription: This test validates that users can personalize their Functional Test Insights experience through options such as column selection, default filters, display density, and other customization settings, and that these preferences persist across sessions.
prerequisites:
1. User is logged into the system with appropriate permissions.
2. Playwright functional tests have been executed and results are available.
3. User has navigated to the Functional Test Insights view.
stepsToPerform:
1. Locate customization options or settings in the Functional Tests Insights view.
2. Modify column visibility by hiding a non-essential column.
3. Change the display density setting (if available).
4. Modify default sorting preference.
5. Save customization settings if required.
6. Navigate away from the Insights view and then return.
7. Verify that customizations have been preserved.
8. Log out and log back in to verify persistence across sessions.
9. Reset all customizations to default settings.
10. Verify that the view returns to its default state.
expectedResult:
1. Customization options should be accessible and clearly labeled.
2. Column visibility changes should immediately reflect in the display.
3. Display density changes should adjust the layout appropriately.
4. Sorting preferences should be applied correctly and maintained.
5. All customizations should persist when navigating away and returning.
6. Customizations should persist across user sessions (after logout/login).
7. Reset functionality should correctly restore all default settings.
8. Customization options should not interfere with core functionality.
9. Changes should be user-specific and not affect other users.
10. Appropriate feedback should be provided when settings are changed or saved.
testData: Test results with sufficient columns and data for meaningful customization
automationNotes: Use Playwright to interact with customization controls. For persistence testing, implement logout/login sequences and verify state is maintained. Test with multiple user accounts to verify user-specific settings.

title: Verify Error Handling and Recovery in Functional Test Insights View
description: Verify that the Functional Test Insights view handles errors gracefully and provides appropriate recovery options
testDescription: This test validates that the Functional Test Insights view handles various error conditions gracefully, displays appropriate error messages to users, and provides recovery mechanisms without crashing or losing user data.
prerequisites:
1. User is logged into the system with appropriate permissions.
2. Functional Test Insights view is configured in the system.
stepsToPerform:
1. Simulate a network error during data loading by disconnecting network temporarily.
2. Observe error handling behavior and messaging.
3. Verify the presence of a retry option and use it after reconnecting.
4. Simulate an invalid filter combination that returns no results.
5. Check for appropriate 'no results' messaging.
6. Attempt to access a non-existent test details page directly via URL.
7. Verify error handling for missing test data.
8. Simulate server errors by accessing the view with invalid parameters (if possible).
9. Test behavior when attempting to export an extremely large dataset.
10. Verify recovery after browser refresh during various operations.
expectedResult:
1. Network errors should display user-friendly error messages explaining the issue.
2. Retry options should be provided where appropriate.
3. No results from filtering should show clear messaging rather than empty space.
4. Invalid direct URLs should display appropriate error messages and navigation options.
5. Server errors should be handled gracefully with meaningful error messages.
6. The system should not crash or become unusable after encountering errors.
7. User input and state should be preserved where possible after error recovery.
8. Error messages should be clearly visible and descriptive.
9. Technical error details should be available but not overwhelming for regular users.
10. Performance degradation handling should provide feedback during slow operations.
testData: Various error conditions (network issues, invalid filters, non-existent resources)
automationNotes: Use Playwright's network interception capabilities to simulate network errors. For server errors, may need specific test endpoints or parameters. Document any manual setup required for certain error conditions.

title: Verify Cross-Environment Test Result Comparison
description: Verify that users can compare Playwright functional test results across different environments and configurations
testDescription: This test validates that the Functional Test Insights view allows users to compare test results across different environments (development, staging, production), browser configurations, and device types to identify environment-specific issues.
prerequisites:
1. User is logged into the system with appropriate permissions.
2. Playwright tests have been executed across multiple environments and configurations.
3. User has navigated to the Functional Test Insights view.
stepsToPerform:
1. Locate environment or configuration comparison features in the Insights view.
2. Select two different environments (e.g., staging vs. production).
3. Initiate a comparison of test results between the selected environments.
4. Examine the comparison view for differences in test status across environments.
5. Identify tests that pass in one environment but fail in another.
6. Select two different browser configurations for comparison.
7. Compare test results between different browsers to identify browser-specific issues.
8. If available, compare results between different device types (desktop vs. mobile).
9. Verify the ability to export comparison results.
expectedResult:
1. Environment/configuration comparison features should be easily accessible.
2. Comparison view should clearly highlight differences between environments.
3. Tests with different statuses across environments should be prominently displayed.
4. Detailed information should be available for tests that behave differently across environments.
5. Browser-specific issues should be easily identifiable in comparison views.
6. Device-specific issues should be clearly indicated if device testing is supported.
7. Comparison data should be accurate and reflect the actual differences in test results.
8. Multiple comparison dimensions should be supported (environment, browser, device).
9. Export of comparison results should include all relevant differential data.
testData: Test results from multiple environments, browsers, and device configurations with some environment-specific failures
automationNotes: Use Playwright to interact with comparison features. May require specific test data setup with environment-specific results. Verify accurate highlighting of differences using expect() assertions.

title: Verify Real-Time Updates of Functional Test Results
description: Verify that the Functional Test Insights view can display real-time updates of test results as tests are being executed
testDescription: This test validates that the Functional Test Insights view can receive and display real-time updates when Playwright tests are being executed, allowing users to monitor ongoing test runs without manually refreshing the page.
prerequisites:
1. User is logged into the system with appropriate permissions.
2. A mechanism exists to run Playwright tests while viewing the Insights page.
3. User has navigated to the Functional Test Insights view.
stepsToPerform:
1. Identify or enable any 'live update' or 'real-time' mode in the Insights view.
2. Initiate a new Playwright test run while keeping the Insights view open.
3. Observe the Insights view for indications of tests in progress.
4. Verify that test statuses update in real-time as tests complete.
5. Check for visual indicators of currently running tests.
6. Verify that summary statistics update as test results come in.
7. If a test fails during execution, verify that it appears in the failed tests section.
8. Monitor real-time updates for performance metrics as they become available.
9. If supported, check for streaming logs from currently executing tests.
10. Verify that the view remains responsive during updates.
expectedResult:
1. Real-time update mode should be clearly indicated when active.
2. In-progress tests should be visually distinguished from completed tests.
3. Test results should appear in the view as they complete, without manual refresh.
4. Status changes should be visually apparent (animations, color changes, etc.).
5. Summary statistics should update automatically as results come in.
6. Failed tests should immediately appear in the appropriate sections.
7. Real-time updates should not cause UI performance issues or excessive resource usage.
8. Connection issues during real-time updates should be handled gracefully.
9. If supported, logs from currently running tests should stream in real-time.
10. The system should indicate when all tests have completed execution.
testData: Ongoing Playwright test execution that can be triggered while viewing the Insights page
automationNotes: This test may require specific setup to trigger test runs during the test. May need to use Playwright's ability to launch subprocesses or API calls to initiate test runs. For verification, monitor DOM changes using mutation observers or polling.

title: Verify Authentication and Authorization for Functional Test Insights View
description: Verify that access to the Functional Test Insights view follows proper authentication and authorization rules
testDescription: This test validates that the Functional Test Insights view enforces appropriate authentication and authorization controls, ensuring that only authorized users can access the view and that permission levels correctly determine which actions users can perform.
prerequisites:
1. Multiple user accounts with different permission levels are set up in the system.
2. Playwright functional tests have been executed and results are available.
3. Authentication system is properly configured with various role-based permissions.
stepsToPerform:
1. Attempt to access the Functional Test Insights view without logging in.
2. Verify redirect to login page or access denied message.
3. Log in with a user account that has read-only permissions.
4. Navigate to the Functional Test Insights view.
5. Verify that view-only actions are available but modification actions are not.
6. Attempt actions that should require elevated permissions and verify they are blocked.
7. Log out and log in with an administrator account.
8. Navigate to the Functional Test Insights view.
9. Verify that all actions including configuration changes are available.
10. Log out and log in with a user who has no permissions for test insights.
11. Attempt to navigate to the Functional Test Insights view.
expectedResult:
1. Unauthenticated access attempts should redirect to login page or show access denied.
2. Read-only users should be able to view test results but not modify configurations.
3. Read-only users should not see admin-only controls or they should be disabled.
4. Admin users should have access to all functionality including configuration options.
5. Users without test insights permissions should not be able to access the view at all.
6. Permission-based UI elements should be consistently applied (hidden/disabled).
7. Permission changes should take effect without requiring application restart.
8. Authentication status should be clearly indicated in the UI.
testData: User accounts with various permission levels (admin, read-only, no-access)
automationNotes: Use Playwright's authentication handling to test different user accounts. Store credentials securely or use test accounts. Verify UI state and available actions with expect() assertions.

title: Verify Responsive Design of Functional Test Insights View
description: Verify that the Functional Test Insights view is properly responsive across various screen sizes and devices
testDescription: This test validates that the Functional Test Insights view implements responsive design principles and functions properly across a range of device sizes from mobile to large desktop displays, ensuring a consistent user experience regardless of device.
prerequisites:
1. User is logged into the system with appropriate permissions.
2. Playwright functional tests have been executed and results are available.
3. User has navigated to the Functional Test Insights view.
stepsToPerform:
1. Set viewport to a large desktop size (e.g., 1920x1080).
2. Verify all components are properly displayed and functional.
3. Resize viewport to a medium desktop/laptop size (e.g., 1366x768).
4. Verify layout adjusts appropriately and all features remain accessible.
5. Resize viewport to tablet dimensions (e.g., 768x1024 portrait).
6. Verify layout adapts to narrower width and all functionality remains accessible.
7. Resize viewport to mobile phone dimensions (e.g., 375x667).
8. Verify layout adapts to mobile view with appropriate navigation patterns.
9. Test interactive elements (filters, details expansion) on each device size.
10. Rotate device orientation for tablet and mobile sizes and verify layout adjusts correctly.
expectedResult:
1. Layout should adjust fluidly between different viewport sizes without broken elements.
2. All functionality should remain accessible across all device sizes.
3. On smaller screens, appropriate UI patterns should be used (hamburger menus, collapsible sections).
4. Text and interactive elements should remain readable and usable at all sizes.
5. Charts and visualizations should adapt to available space while maintaining readability.
6. Tables should implement horizontal scrolling or responsive reflow on small screens.
7. Touch targets should be appropriately sized on touch devices.
8. Orientation changes should be handled gracefully without layout issues.
9. No horizontal scrolling should be required on any screen size (except within contained elements like tables).
10. Performance should remain acceptable on lower-powered mobile devices.
testData: Test results with sufficient data to populate all UI components
automationNotes: Use Playwright's page.setViewportSize() to test different screen dimensions. Capture screenshots at each size for visual verification. Test touch interactions using page.tap() for mobile viewports.

title: Verify Batch Actions for Functional Test Results
description: Verify that users can perform batch actions on multiple functional test results simultaneously
testDescription: This test validates that users can select multiple Playwright functional test results and perform batch actions such as bulk tagging, export, rerun, or status updates, improving efficiency when working with large test suites.
prerequisites:
1. User is logged into the system with appropriate permissions.
2. Multiple Playwright functional tests have been executed with various statuses.
3. User has navigated to the Functional Test Insights view.
stepsToPerform:
1. Locate multi-select functionality in the test results list (checkboxes or similar).
2. Select 3-5 test results using the selection mechanism.
3. Verify visual indication that multiple items are selected.
4. Locate and activate batch action menu or controls.
5. Test batch export functionality and verify all selected tests are included.
6. Select a different set of tests and apply batch tagging functionality.
7. Verify tags are applied to all selected tests.
8. Select a mix of passed and failed tests and use batch rerun functionality if available.
9. Verify the appropriate tests are queued for rerun.
10. Test selection shortcuts (select all, invert selection, select failed) if available.
expectedResult:
1. Multi-select controls should be intuitive and clearly visible.
2. Selected items should be visually distinguished from non-selected items.
3. The number of currently selected items should be displayed.
4. Batch action controls should become available when multiple items are selected.
5. Batch exports should include all selected tests and be properly formatted.
6. Batch tagging should apply tags to all selected tests simultaneously.
7. Batch reruns should correctly queue the selected tests for execution.
8. Selection shortcuts should function correctly and select the appropriate tests.
9. Deselection of individual items and 'clear selection' should work properly.
10. Batch actions should provide appropriate feedback on completion.
testData: Multiple test results with various statuses and characteristics
automationNotes: Use Playwright's locator methods to select multiple elements. May require special handling for checkboxes and custom selection controls. Verify batch operations complete successfully by checking resulting state.

title: Verify Context-Aware Navigation Between Test Types
description: Verify that users can navigate between related tests of different types while maintaining context
testDescription: This test validates that the Functional Test Insights view provides context-aware navigation between related tests of different types (Unit, Integration, API, Functional), allowing users to follow test coverage across the testing pyramid while maintaining relevant context.
prerequisites:
1. User is logged into the system with appropriate permissions.
2. Multiple test types (Unit, Integration, API, Functional) have been executed for related components.
3. User has navigated to the Functional Test Insights view.
stepsToPerform:
1. Locate a functional test that tests a specific feature or component.
2. Identify any indicators showing related tests of other types.
3. Click on a link or navigate to related unit tests for the same component.
4. Verify that appropriate context is maintained (component focus, filtering).
5. Navigate to related integration tests from the current view.
6. Verify context is preserved and relevant tests are displayed.
7. Navigate to related API tests that cover the same functionality.
8. Return to the original functional test using breadcrumbs or navigation aids.
9. Verify that the system maintains a navigation history for cross-test-type exploration.
10. Test any visualization that shows test coverage across test types for a component.
expectedResult:
1. Related tests of different types should be indicated or discoverable from a test details view.
2. Navigation between test types should maintain context about the component or feature.
3. When navigating between test types, appropriate filters should be automatically applied.
4. Breadcrumbs or similar navigation aids should show the current path across test types.
5. Navigation history should be maintained allowing backward/forward navigation.
6. Coverage visualization (if available) should accurately show test distribution across types.
7. The relationship between different test types should be clearly indicated.
8. Performance should remain good when navigating between different test type views.
9. Context should be maintained even after page refreshes if possible.
10. Any applied filters or search terms should be appropriately translated between views.
testData: Related tests of different types (Unit, Integration, API, Functional) for the same components
automationNotes: Use Playwright's navigation methods and verify context preservation by checking URL parameters, applied filters, and selected elements after navigation. May require setting up related tests across different types beforehand.

title: Verify Visual Regression Testing Integration in Insights View
description: Verify that visual regression test results are properly integrated into the Functional Test Insights view
testDescription: This test validates that visual regression testing results from Playwright are properly integrated into the Functional Test Insights view, allowing users to visually compare expected vs. actual screenshots and identify visual regressions.
prerequisites:
1. User is logged into the system with appropriate permissions.
2. Playwright tests with visual comparison assertions have been executed.
3. Some tests have visual differences detected.
4. User has navigated to the Functional Test Insights view.
stepsToPerform:
1. Locate tests with visual comparison results in the Insights view.
2. Identify visual indicators that distinguish tests with visual differences.
3. Open details for a test with visual differences detected.
4. Locate and open the visual comparison tool/viewer.
5. Verify the expected vs. actual images are displayed side by side.
6. Test any image comparison features (slider, diff highlight, zoom).
7. If available, check visual history to see previous versions of the screenshot.
8. Verify ability to approve a visual change as the new baseline.
9. Test any annotation or commenting features for visual differences.
10. Verify that approved changes update the baseline for future test runs.
expectedResult:
1. Tests with visual differences should be clearly marked in the test results list.
2. Visual comparison viewer should load quickly and display images at high quality.
3. Side-by-side comparison should clearly show differences between expected and actual.
4. Diff highlighting should accurately indicate areas with visual differences.
5. Image manipulation tools (zoom, pan) should function correctly.
6. Approval workflow should be intuitive and function correctly.
7. Approved changes should be reflected in subsequent test runs.
8. Full-resolution images should be available for detailed inspection.
9. The system should handle various image sizes and formats correctly.
10. Performance should remain good when viewing large or multiple images.
testData: Playwright tests with visual comparison assertions and detected differences
automationNotes: Use Playwright to navigate to visual comparison features. May require specific test setup with known visual differences. Verify image loading and comparison features using expect() assertions on visibility and content.

title: Verify Data Persistence for User Preferences in Functional Test Insights
description: Verify that user preferences and configurations for the Functional Test Insights view are properly saved and persisted
testDescription: This test validates that any user preferences configured in the Functional Test Insights view (column layouts, filter preferences, display settings) are properly saved and persisted when the user returns to the view after navigation or logout/login cycles.
prerequisites:
1. User is logged into the system with appropriate permissions.
2. Functional Test Insights view is available with configurable preferences.
3. Multiple Playwright test results are available in the system.
stepsToPerform:
1. Navigate to the Functional Test Insights view.
2. Configure column visibility by hiding a specific column.
3. Apply a specific sort order to the test results.
4. Set a custom filter combination.
5. Navigate away to a different section of the application.
6. Return to the Functional Test Insights view.
7. Verify all configured preferences are maintained.
8. Log out of the application.
9. Log back in with the same user.
10. Navigate to the Functional Test Insights view and verify preferences are still applied.
expectedResult:
1. All user preferences should be maintained when navigating away and returning to the view.
2. Hidden columns should remain hidden upon return.
3. Sort order should be preserved exactly as configured.
4. Filter combinations should remain applied.
5. Preferences should persist across user sessions (logout/login).
6. Changes to preferences should be user-specific and not affect other users' views.
7. The system should apply the saved preferences immediately when the view loads.
testData: User account with permission to modify view preferences
automationNotes: Use localStorage or cookies inspection to verify preference storage mechanism. Test persistence across page refreshes, navigation events, and complete session cycles.

title: Verify Bulk Test Execution Triggering from Insights View
description: Verify that users can trigger bulk re-execution of selected Playwright tests directly from the Functional Test Insights view
testDescription: This test validates that users can select multiple test cases from the Functional Test Insights view and trigger their re-execution, and that the system properly handles the execution request and updates the results when complete.
prerequisites:
1. User is logged into the system with appropriate permissions to execute tests.
2. Multiple Playwright test results are available in the Functional Test Insights view.
3. The test execution infrastructure is operational.
stepsToPerform:
1. Navigate to the Functional Test Insights view.
2. Select multiple test cases using the multi-select functionality.
3. Locate and click the 'Re-run Selected Tests' or equivalent button.
4. Verify that a confirmation dialog appears.
5. Confirm the execution request.
6. Observe any execution status indicators or progress information.
7. Wait for test execution to complete or verify that it has been queued.
8. Refresh or monitor the Insights view for updated test results.
9. Verify that the re-executed tests show updated execution times and results.
10. Check that test history correctly shows the previous and new execution results.
expectedResult:
1. Multi-select functionality should allow selection of specific tests for re-execution.
2. The system should provide clear confirmation before triggering execution.
3. Execution request should be properly received and processed by the test infrastructure.
4. Users should receive feedback about the execution status (queued, in-progress, complete).
5. After execution, results should be updated with the latest execution data.
6. Test history should maintain records of both previous and new executions.
7. If execution fails to start, appropriate error messages should be displayed.
8. The system should handle large numbers of selected tests appropriately.
testData: Multiple test cases that can be re-executed
automationNotes: May require special test environment setup to allow actual test execution. Consider using mocked responses for execution requests in some test scenarios. Verify with both passing and failing test cases.

title: Verify Tag Management for Functional Test Results
description: Verify that users can add, remove, and filter by custom tags on Playwright functional test results
testDescription: This test validates that users can create and apply custom tags to Playwright test results for better organization and filtering, and that these tags persist and function correctly for search and filtering operations.
prerequisites:
1. User is logged into the system with appropriate permissions.
2. Multiple Playwright functional test results are available in the system.
3. User has navigated to the Functional Test Insights view.
stepsToPerform:
1. Locate a specific test result in the Functional Test Insights view.
2. Identify and click on tag management functionality for this test.
3. Add a new custom tag (e.g., 'critical-path').
4. Verify the tag appears associated with the test.
5. Add the same tag to several other test results.
6. Use the filtering functionality to filter by the newly created tag.
7. Verify only tests with that tag are displayed.
8. Remove the tag from one of the tests.
9. Refresh the filter to verify the update.
10. Create multiple tags and test combination filtering with multiple tags.
expectedResult:
1. Tag management interface should be intuitive and accessible.
2. Creating new tags should be straightforward with visual feedback.
3. Tags should be immediately associated with the selected test.
4. Filtering by tags should work accurately, showing only tagged tests.
5. Multiple tags should be supported for a single test.
6. Tag removal should be confirmed and immediately reflected.
7. Tags should persist across page refreshes and user sessions.
8. The system should support filtering by multiple tags (AND/OR logic).
9. Tag colors or visual indicators should be consistent throughout the interface.
10. Performance should remain good even with many tags applied.
testData: Multiple test results that can be tagged
automationNotes: Test tag persistence by verifying database storage or making API calls to confirm server-side storage. For complex tag filtering, test various combinations of AND/OR logic if supported.

title: Verify Deep Linking to Specific Test Results and Filters
description: Verify that deep links to specific test results or filtered views work correctly in the Functional Test Insights view
testDescription: This test validates that users can share direct links to specific test results or filtered views within the Functional Test Insights view, and that these links correctly restore the exact state when accessed.
prerequisites:
1. User is logged into the system with appropriate permissions.
2. Multiple Playwright functional test results are available in the system.
3. The Functional Test Insights view supports URL parameters for state management.
stepsToPerform:
1. Navigate to the Functional Test Insights view.
2. Apply specific filters (e.g., failed tests in Chrome from last 7 days).
3. Copy the current URL from the browser address bar.
4. Open a new browser tab and paste the URL.
5. Verify the same filtered view is displayed.
6. Navigate to a specific test's detailed view.
7. Copy the URL from the address bar.
8. Open a new browser tab and paste the URL.
9. Verify the same test detail view is displayed.
10. Create a complex state (filtered view plus expanded test) and test deep linking.
11. Try accessing deep links from a logged-out state to verify authentication handling.
expectedResult:
1. URLs should contain parameters that capture the current filter state.
2. Opening a deep link should restore exactly the same filtered view.
3. Test detail deep links should navigate directly to the specific test's details.
4. Complex state deep links should restore multiple aspects of the view state.
5. When accessing deep links while logged out, the system should redirect to login and then restore the intended view.
6. Sharing deep links between different browsers should work correctly.
7. Deep links should remain functional across application updates.
8. Invalid parameters in deep links should be handled gracefully.
9. Deep links should work with all supported browsers.
10. Performance should not be significantly impacted when resolving complex deep link states.
testData: Various filtered views and specific test results to link to
automationNotes: Use Playwright's ability to open multiple browser contexts to test link sharing. Verify URL parameter handling and state restoration. Test with both valid and invalid parameters to ensure robust error handling.

title: Verify Multi-Language Support in Functional Test Insights View
description: Verify that the Functional Test Insights view properly supports multiple languages and localization
testDescription: This test validates that the Functional Test Insights view correctly displays content in different languages based on user preferences, and that all functionality works correctly regardless of the selected language.
prerequisites:
1. User is logged into the system with appropriate permissions.
2. The application supports multiple languages/locales.
3. Playwright functional test results are available in the system.
4. User has the ability to change language preferences.
stepsToPerform:
1. Navigate to the Functional Test Insights view with default language settings.
2. Note key UI elements and their labels/text.
3. Change the application language to a different supported language.
4. Verify that UI elements in the Functional Test Insights view are translated.
5. Test core functionality (filtering, sorting, expanding test details) in the non-default language.
6. Verify that test result content displays correctly with non-Latin characters.
7. Check that date/time formats follow the selected locale's conventions.
8. Test search functionality with non-Latin characters if applicable.
9. Verify that error messages are displayed in the selected language.
10. Return to the default language and verify the interface reverts correctly.
expectedResult:
1. All UI elements should be properly translated in supported languages.
2. Non-Latin characters should display correctly without encoding issues.
3. Date and time formats should follow locale-specific conventions.
4. All functionality should work identically regardless of selected language.
5. Search should function correctly with non-Latin characters.
6. Error messages should be localized to the selected language.
7. Dynamic content should be properly localized.
8. Right-to-left language support should display correctly if applicable.
9. Language changes should be applied immediately without requiring page reload.
10. The selected language preference should persist across user sessions.
tags: localization, internationalization, multi-language, i18n, l10n, accessibility
testData: Test results containing various character sets and languages
automationNotes: Test with at least 2-3 different languages including one with non-Latin characters. Verify text rendering and functionality using expect() assertions. May need to set specific language preferences before tests.

title: Verify Alert and Notification System for Test Status Changes
description: Verify that the Functional Test Insights view provides appropriate alerts and notifications when test statuses change between runs
testDescription: This test validates that the Functional Test Insights view provides timely alerts and notifications when test statuses change between runs, ensuring users are informed of regression issues or resolved problems without manually comparing results.
prerequisites:
1. User is logged into the system with appropriate permissions.
2. Multiple runs of the same Playwright functional tests have been executed with some status changes between runs.
3. Alert configuration for test status changes is enabled in the system.
stepsToPerform:
1. Navigate to the Functional Test Insights view.
2. Identify any visual indicators or notifications for tests that have changed status.
3. Locate a test that has changed from passing to failing in recent runs.
4. Verify that appropriate highlighting or alert indicators are displayed for this test.
5. Check for any notification center or alert summary showing aggregated status changes.
6. If supported, adjust notification settings for test status changes.
7. Trigger a new test run that changes the status of a test.
8. Verify that real-time or refresh-based notifications appear for the status change.
9. Check if email or external notifications are sent for critical status changes.
10. Verify that cleared or resolved status changes are appropriately marked.
expectedResult:
1. Tests with status changes should be visually highlighted in the test results list.
2. The system should clearly differentiate between new failures and ongoing failures.
3. An alert summary or notification center should show aggregated status changes.
4. Critical status changes (passing to failing) should have more prominent alerts than others.
5. Notifications should include relevant details about when and how the status changed.
6. Users should be able to configure notification preferences if supported.
7. Status change indicators should be consistent across the entire Insights view.
8. Historical status changes should be accessible through test history views.
9. Notification mechanisms should work reliably without excessive notifications.
10. Performance should not be significantly impacted by the notification system.
testData: Test results with documented status changes between runs
automationNotes: Use Playwright to verify presence and visibility of notification elements. May need to simulate test status changes or use pre-configured test data. Verify notification appearance using expect() assertions.

title: Verify Test Case Documentation Integration in Insights View
description: Verify that the Functional Test Insights view properly integrates with test case documentation and requirements traceability
testDescription: This test validates that the Functional Test Insights view provides proper integration with test case documentation and requirements traceability, showing relationships between test results and their corresponding requirements, specifications, or user stories.
prerequisites:
1. User is logged into the system with appropriate permissions.
2. Playwright tests with documentation references have been executed.
3. Test case documentation and requirements are maintained in the system.
4. User has navigated to the Functional Test Insights view.
stepsToPerform:
1. Locate a test result in the Functional Test Insights view.
2. Look for indicators showing links to test case documentation or requirements.
3. Click on a documentation link and verify it navigates to the correct document.
4. Verify any requirements or user story identifiers displayed with the test.
5. Navigate to a test with traceability information and examine the details.
6. If available, use filtering to show only tests related to a specific requirement.
7. Check for bidirectional traceability by navigating from requirements to tests.
8. Verify that test coverage metrics for requirements are accurately displayed.
9. Check that documentation links remain valid after test re-execution.
10. Verify proper handling of tests without associated documentation.
expectedResult:
1. Tests should display clear links to their associated documentation.
2. Documentation links should navigate to the correct documents or requirements.
3. Requirement identifiers should be clearly displayed with relevant tests.
4. Filtering by requirement should show all tests associated with that requirement.
5. Coverage metrics should accurately reflect tested requirements.
6. Bidirectional navigation between tests and requirements should work correctly.
7. Documentation integration should not impact performance of the Insights view.
8. Changes to documentation should be reflected in the Insights view appropriately.
9. Tests without documentation should be clearly indicated as such.
10. Documentation links should open in appropriate contexts (same/new tab as configured).
testData: Test results with associated documentation references and requirement IDs
automationNotes: Verify documentation links using page.click() and page.url() to confirm correct navigation. May need to set up test environment with sample documentation references.

title: Verify Custom Metric Tracking for Functional Tests
description: Verify that custom metrics defined in Playwright tests are properly captured and displayed in the Insights view
testDescription: This test validates that custom metrics defined and collected during Playwright test execution (such as page load times, component render times, or custom performance markers) are properly captured, stored, and displayed in the Functional Test Insights view.
prerequisites:
1. User is logged into the system with appropriate permissions.
2. Playwright tests with custom metric collection have been executed.
3. The system is configured to capture and store custom metrics.
4. User has navigated to the Functional Test Insights view.
stepsToPerform:
1. Locate a test with custom metrics in the Functional Test Insights view.
2. Expand the test details to view custom metrics section.
3. Verify that all expected custom metrics are displayed with correct values.
4. Check for appropriate formatting of different metric types (time durations, counts, sizes).
5. If available, examine metric trend visualization across test runs.
6. Verify that metrics can be sorted or filtered based on their values.
7. Check for any threshold indicators for metrics exceeding expected values.
8. If supported, customize the metrics display to show specific metrics of interest.
9. Export the metrics data and verify the export contains all custom metrics.
10. Verify that metric names and values display correctly for various data types.
expectedResult:
1. Custom metrics should be clearly displayed in the test details view.
2. Metric values should be formatted appropriately based on their type.
3. Trends in metrics across test runs should be visualized if supported.
4. Metric thresholds should be clearly indicated when values exceed limits.
5. All custom metrics defined in tests should be captured and displayed.
6. Metric display should be consistent across different browsers and test types.
7. Metrics export should include all custom metric data in appropriate format.
8. Performance of the Insights view should not be degraded by custom metrics display.
9. Large numbers of metrics should be handled with appropriate UI patterns.
10. Metric names with special characters should display correctly.
testData: Test results with various custom metrics recorded
automationNotes: Use Playwright to locate and verify metric elements in the UI. Compare displayed values with expected metric values. Test with various metric types and edge cases (very large values, negative values, etc.).

title: Verify Test Environment Information Display
description: Verify that the Functional Test Insights view properly displays test environment information for Playwright tests
testDescription: This test validates that the Functional Test Insights view accurately displays relevant test environment information for Playwright tests, including browser versions, operating systems, viewport sizes, and other execution context details.
prerequisites:
1. User is logged into the system with appropriate permissions.
2. Playwright tests have been executed across various environments and configurations.
3. Environment details are captured during test execution.
4. User has navigated to the Functional Test Insights view.
stepsToPerform:
1. Locate a test result in the Functional Test Insights view.
2. Expand the test details to view environment information section.
3. Verify that browser name and version are correctly displayed.
4. Check that operating system information is accurately shown.
5. Verify that viewport size used during test execution is displayed.
6. Check for display of other relevant environment factors (device emulation, network conditions).
7. Compare environment information across multiple test results for consistency.
8. If applicable, filter test results by specific environment characteristics.
9. Verify that environment information is included in exported test results.
10. For tests run on multiple environments, verify that all environments are listed.
expectedResult:
1. Environment information should be clearly displayed for each test result.
2. Browser details should include name and exact version number.
3. OS information should include platform and version as applicable.
4. Viewport dimensions should be displayed in appropriate format.
5. Additional environment factors should be clearly labeled and formatted.
6. Environment information should be consistent with the actual execution context.
7. Filtering by environment characteristics should work correctly if supported.
8. Environment details should be included in all export formats.
9. For multi-environment tests, all environments should be properly listed.
10. Environment information display should be consistent across test types.
testData: Test results executed across different browsers, operating systems, and viewport sizes
automationNotes: Verify environment information accuracy by comparing displayed values with known execution environments. Test with various browser versions and operating systems if possible.

title: Verify Test Flakiness Detection and Reporting
description: Verify that the Functional Test Insights view correctly identifies and reports flaky Playwright tests
testDescription: This test validates that the Functional Test Insights view can identify patterns of inconsistent test results (flaky tests), properly flag them, and provide insights to help diagnose and address test flakiness issues.
prerequisites:
1. User is logged into the system with appropriate permissions.
2. Multiple runs of the same Playwright tests have been executed.
3. Some tests have inconsistent results across runs (sometimes passing, sometimes failing).
4. User has navigated to the Functional Test Insights view.
stepsToPerform:
1. Locate indicators for flaky tests in the Functional Test Insights view.
2. Identify a test that has been flagged as flaky.
3. Examine the flakiness details to see the pattern of inconsistent results.
4. Check for flakiness rate or percentage indication.
5. Verify that test history shows the alternating pass/fail pattern.
6. If available, examine any automated analysis of potential flakiness causes.
7. Filter to show only flaky tests and verify the filter works correctly.
8. Check if flaky tests are distinguished from consistently failing tests in reports.
9. Verify that flakiness information is included in exported data.
10. If supported, check for recommendations to reduce test flakiness.
expectedResult:
1. Flaky tests should be clearly indicated with distinct visual markers.
2. Flakiness rate or percentage should be accurately calculated and displayed.
3. Test history should clearly show the pattern of inconsistent results.
4. Filtering for flaky tests should show only tests with inconsistent results.
5. Reports should distinguish between flaky tests and consistently failing tests.
6. Any flakiness analysis should provide relevant information for debugging.
7. Flaky test indicators should be consistent across the Insights view.
8. Flakiness information should be included in exports and reports.
9. If available, recommendations for addressing flakiness should be relevant.
10. The system should use appropriate thresholds to identify truly flaky tests.
testData: Test results with documented inconsistent results across multiple runs
automationNotes: May need to specifically set up flaky test results or simulate flakiness patterns in the test data. Verify flakiness indicators using expect() assertions on visibility and content.
